content: Dr. Rachel Hammonds, from the Law and Development Research Group at the University of Antwerp in Belgium, specializes in health equity, behavioral science, and program evaluation. Dr. Renuka Jayatissa, affiliated with the Department of Nutrition at the Medical Research Institute under the Ministry of Health in Sri Lanka, focuses on micronutrients, public health, and clinical nutrition. Dr. Crystal Karakochuk, from the Faculty of Land and Food Systems at the University of British Columbia in Canada, is an expert in diagnostic methods and biomarkers for anemia. Dr. Heimo Mairbäurl, based at the German Center for Lung Research at the University Hospital Heidelberg in Germany, studies the physiology of hemoglobin changes at high altitudes. Dr. Lynnette Neufeld, representing the Global Alliance for Improved Nutrition in Switzerland, has expertise in nutrition, micronutrient programs, public health, and epidemiology. Dr. Tarek Owaidah, from the Department of Pathology and Laboratory Medicine at King Faisal Specialist Hospital & Research Center in Saudi Arabia, specializes in blood banks and transfusions. Dr. Kamija Phiri, from the College of Medicine at the University of Malawi, focuses on malaria, hematology, global health, and epidemiology. Dr. Harshpal Singh Sachdev, affiliated with the Sitaram Bhartia Institute of Science and Research in India, is an expert in maternal and child nutrition, epidemiology, and pediatrics. Dr. Elizabeth Tejero, from the Laboratory of Nutrigenomics and Nutrigenetics at the National Institute for Genomic Medicine in Mexico, studies genetic variation and nutritional status. Dr. Vip Viprakasit, from the Faculty of Medicine at Mahidol University in Thailand, specializes in genetics, hemoglobinopathies, and clinical practice. Professor Pattanee Winichagoon, also from Mahidol University in Thailand, focuses on micronutrients, iron metabolism, and thalassemias. Professor Erica Wood, from the Transfusion Research Unit at Monash University in Australia, is an expert in hematology, hemovigilance, blood safety, and clinical practice. Dr. Melissa F. Young, from the Hubert Department of Global Health at Emory University in the United States, specializes in anemia, micronutrients, maternal and child nutrition, epidemiology, and program evaluation. Dr. Crystal Karakochuk was unable to attend the first Guideline Development Group (GDG) meeting. Professor Beverly-Ann Biggs and Dr. Lynnette Neufeld could not continue as GDG members after the first meeting. Dr. Rachel Hammonds served as a GDG member until November 21, 2022, and participated in the first and second GDG meetings. Dr. Eric Ohuma, from the Centre for Tropical Medicine and Global Health at the University of Oxford in the United Kingdom, specializes in medical statistics. Dr. Erica Ota, from the Graduate School of Nursing Science at St. Luke’s International University in Japan, focuses on nutrition and systematic reviews. Professor Sant-Rayn Pasricha, from the Population Health and Immunity Division at the Walter and Eliza Hall Institute of Medical Research in Australia, is a hematology scientist and clinician. Dr. Andrea Sharma, from the Division of Nutrition, Physical Activity, and Obesity at the United States Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, specializes in nutrition and epidemiology. The systematic review teams contributed to technical presentations and discussions, providing factual information, feedback, and clarifications when required. However, they did not participate in or influence decision-making processes. Dr. Omar Dary, from the Bureau of Global Health at the US Agency for International Development, and Dr. Sorrel Namaste, from the Demographic and Health Surveys Program in the United States, served as peer reviewers. Dr. Nelly Zavaleta, from the Instituto de Investigación Nutricional in Peru, and Dr. Michael Zimmermann, from the Institute of Food, Nutrition, and Health at the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology in Switzerland, also contributed as peer reviewers. It is noted that the acknowledgment of peer reviewers does not imply their endorsement of the normative statements in the guideline, nor does it necessarily represent the views, decisions, or policies of their affiliated institutions.
